text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel on Tuesday condemned the expulsion over the weekend of hundreds of returning Bosnian refugees by a Bosnian Croat mob and called on Croatian President Franjo Tudjman to condemn it too.
"What happened in (the central Bosnian town of) Jajce was disgraceful. Yet again, houses of returning refugees were set on fire, with one person dying as a result," Kinkel said in a statement.

"I expect President Tudjman to condemn these events in Jajce," he added, noting that Tudjman was due to meet Alija Izetbegovic, president of Bosnia's collective presidency, in the Adriatic port of Split on Wednesday.

Earlier on Tuesday, the United Nations refugee agency detailed how a "drunken Croatian mob" had over the weekend expelled some 300 Moslems seeking to return to their homes in and around Jajce, which is 98 percent Bosnian Croat.
Bosnian television reported one man had been burned to death after his home was torched.
Under the Dayton pact which ended the 1992-95 Bosnian war, all refugees in the former Yugoslavia have a right to their pre-war homes.
But the majority of the 260,000 Bosnian refugees in Germany come from minority areas of the region, thus increasing the chance of local resistance to their return.

Kinkel said he would be suspending the one million marks ($536,000) of reconstruction aid promised by Germany for projects in Jajce and recommending that European Union funds for similar projects there also be frozen. ($ = 1.863 German Marks)
